page: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates moderate CPU capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests yield average performance scores of 1519.79 and 6053.66 respectively. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, reaching 71.99 GB/sec for read-only operations and 35.14 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in memory-bound tasks with small blocks and in Geekbench single-core and multi-core suites. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-accelerated AES, though Passmark encryption scores are relatively low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers a high density of dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, offering predictable compute performance for its resource class. Given the compute-to-memory ratio and lack of local storage, this instance is suited for distributed compute workloads, containerized microservices, static web serving, and basic database operations that do not require high-performance local disk access or massive memory footprints.

It is configured with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results show average performance in stress-ng CPU tests and large-block memory bandwidth, alongside weaker metrics in Geekbench and single-threaded compression tasks. With hardware-accelerated AES cryptography and dedicated core allocation, the c6g.xlarge offers a cost-efficient, predictable compute profile for ARM-native applications. It is best suited for workloads such as containerized microservices, static web serving, and moderate database operations.
